bits-lamps.note: THE BITS JACK KEEPS ITS TWO LAMPS AS SEPARATE PLACEMENTS, and it is the only jack in the library that does. The RJ45 family (docs/rj45-family-design.md, #125) has four members - two bare, two lamped - and no bare-with-lamps one. BITS is a timing role, so decision 3 puts it on std/rj45@2, the bare housing; but the hardware guide draws a link and an activity lamp beside it, so led-bits-link and led-bits-act stay where they are, naming the jack with for:, the same shape edgecore/as5912-54x uses for its mgmt-eth pair. One jack does not earn a fifth family member. L76 does not count this as an unlamped Ethernet jack (BITS is not Ethernet) and L39 lets the lamps sit inside the jack's own cutout; if a second bare-with-lamps jack ever arrives, the family gains a member.

chassis.note: datasheet-table - Table 19: chassis 1.72 x 19 x 18.50 in (43.7 x 482.3 x 470 mm), 1RU; the dimension drawing g009881 (top view) reads the width as 18.99 in (48.23 cm) and the depth over fan and power handles as 20.41 in (51.84 cm) against Table 19's 20.43. The rack-requirements table says the MOUNTING BRACKETS "extend the width to 19 in", yet drawing and table agree the body itself is ~482.3 including the integral ear flanges - this chassis is genuinely full-rack-width, with the front face spanning ear to ear. The modelled width is the 437.0 mm BODY between the ear-flange fold lines (ears are not modelled here - see ears)

color.note: photo - light Juniper grey, sampled from mx204-front-high.jpg (#9a9ea3); module faces near-black charcoal, fan furniture orange

drawing-vs-photo.note: sources-disagree, and the REAL DEVICE (Juniper studio photographs) wins for everything printed: the guide art labels the QSFP ports 0/0-0/3 and the SFP+ ports 1/0-1/7 (CLI interface names), prints 10MHz / 1PPS on the SMB columns, orders the LED row ...SSD1 SSD0, puts MX204 beside the Juniper logo and a junos badge at the right. The photographed faceplate prints plain 0-3 and 4/5-10/11 port numbers, PPS and 100MHz under the SMB columns, orders the row SSD0 SSD1, prints MX204 at the RIGHT end and carries no junos badge. The silkscreen below follows the photograph; note the guide TEXT unambiguously calls the clock ports 10-MHz (pinout table, clocking topic), so the printed 100MHz legend is carried as artwork while the function stays 10 MHz - see gaps

ears.note: NOT MODELLED, by project convention - devices in this library are drawn without rack ears. The MX204's guide art draws integral ear flanges at both ends of both faces (fold lines at x 22.65 and 459.65 on the 482.3 mm rack face, each flange carrying two rounded slots and, on the front, a central 8.2 mm hole), and Table 19's 19 in width is measured over them. The modelled body is the 437.0 mm between the fold lines; all front and rear coordinates were measured on the 482.3 mm drawing and shifted by -22.65. The removable outboard brackets in the photographs are likewise not modelled

esd-front.note: drawing + photo - a recessed socket at 31.1, 28.9 with the ESD symbol below; the guide's "ESD Points" figure (g009865, Figure 5) marks this same location. The guide art draws it as a hex-nut stud; the photograph shows a plain recessed socket - photo carried

ground-plate.note: the hardware guide, twice: the grounding points are spaced at 0.75-in. (19.1-mm) centres, 3/4 in., 19.05 (Ground the MX204 Router; Grounding Points on the Router, Figure 17). The plate is juniper/mx204-ground-plate@2, which composes two 10-32 screws at exactly 19.05 and presents `stud-pair-3-4`, so one two-hole lug (generic/two-hole-lug-3-4@1) lands across the pair and the ring lug still lands on either screw, `ground-plate/1` and `/2`. @1 drew the holes 16.0 apart off the g009862 render (x 38.6 and 54.6 of the rack face); they moved symmetrically about the same centre, x 23.95, inside the plate, and the plate, its cutout and the earth symbol did not move. The guide also says M5 once where it says 10-32 twice; the `stud-size` is 10-32 and the plate's provenance.thread records the disagreement

ground-stud-size.note: the hardware guide, Grounding Points on the Router: the grounding points are studs sized for 10-32 screws, and two threaded holes fit 10-32 screws: the `stud-size` of the plate's pair. The guide says M5 once elsewhere (provenance.ground-plate)

laser-warning.note: the front laser-safety label is not an earthing point: it moved from `grounding` (rel-pos 4) to its own `furniture` group at rel-pos 0 (#414). The empty silkscreen mark that named it (text '', font-size 0.1) printed nothing and is gone. Where the label sits is the front drawing's reading (provenance.scale), unchanged

other-faces.note: near-blank by evidence - no photograph or drawing of the top, bottom or side faces exists in the intake beyond the g009881 top-view outline, which shows a plain slab with the mounting rails pre-attached along the sides. Each face carries only its rail band(s), estimated and marked so, which is also what lets the capability chain count the face as drawn. Faces are sized from Table 19. Every face carries only symmetric content as far as the sources show, so the axis conventions have been checked but nothing asymmetric pins them. Axis conventions, checked against viewer3d.js: LEFT view x = 0 is the REAR, RIGHT view x = 0 is the FRONT, top and bottom have y = 0 at the FRONT with left/right mirrored between them

port-leds.note: photo + drawing - each SFP+ column carries a lamp strip between the rows: triangle-up, two lenses, triangle-down (drawing shows the four marks at y 22.1 with lenses at column-centre +/-1.8). The up triangle ties the left lens to the upper port and the down triangle the right lens to the lower port. NO DOCUMENT DESCRIBES THESE LAMPS: searched the guide doc.md for "port LED", "link and activity", "rate-selectable" near LED, and "triangle"; the front-panel LED table (Table 17) covers only system LEDs. States left as the component default, description records the silence. The QSFP ports carry NO per-port faceplate LEDs - confirmed against the photograph, not just the text (the only marks above the cages are vent holes). The GM/PTP port has two stacked lamps at x 63.6 (y 26.6/32.1), also undocumented

port-numbering.note: photo - QSFP ports are silkscreened 0-3; SFP+ columns are silkscreened 4/5, 6/7, 8/9, 10/11 with the UPPER number on the upper port (the guide art writes 1/0 over 1/1 the same way up). CLI names (et-0/0/x, xe-0/1/x) are not printed on the metal

port-speeds.note: MGMT is `1g`: the hardware guide describes it as an autosensing RJ-45 supporting 10, 100 or 1000 Mb/s (also carried in `attrs.management.oob`). BITS, ToD and CON state no speed; their media say what they carry (`rj48`, `rj45-tod`, `rj45-serial`). The GM/PTP SFP has no rate anywhere - see gaps.

power.note: guide power planning - 240 W typical at 25 C and 280 W maximum at 55 C for a fully loaded router (Tables 28 and 31, AC and DC alike; the vendor qualifies both by ambient, not by measure). Table 32 adds the DC INPUT figure at 90% efficiency: 266 W at 25 C; Table 33's 55 C input value fell outside the text layer of this extraction and is not carried. Table 20 separately states maximum thermal output 1705 BTU/hour (500 W) - a different scope (provisioning ceiling) that is transcribed under thermal and deliberately NOT reconciled with the 280 W draw

rear.note: drawing (g009862 at the same per-axis scales) + photo - recessed left panel 24-97.7 across the full height carrying the grounding plate (lug circles at 38.6 and 54.6, y 17.2), the earth symbol at 46.6, 31.6 and the ESD socket at 81.4, 17.2 with its symbol above at 81.1, 6.7. Three fan bays with apertures ~42 mm on a 49.1 mm pitch at x 107.8/156.9/206.0, each preceded by a chassis strip printed with a fan icon (y 17.1), the bay number (y 21.6) and the fan status lamp (y 28.9) at x 103.2/152.4/201.2. Two PSU bays at 334.9 and 396.3 (apertures measure 57.0, module width 56.6 per Table 19; the bay is sized 42.4 tall for the DC module, the taller of the two occupants per Table 19, so the 40.1 AC face sits in it with clearance), silkscreened 0 and 1 on the chassis left of each bay. rear-axis.note: the rear view is its own face with x = 0 at ITS left edge (the chassis RIGHT side seen from the front); the fan and PSU modules are horizontal, so nothing mirrors. Positions are direct measurements of the rear drawing, not derived from front coordinates

rj45-orientation.note: drawing + photo - CON and ToD are drawn and photographed contacts-UP (keyway down, std/rj45 default); MGMT and BITS are drawn contacts-DOWN with two integrated LED windows at the top corners, so they carry rotate 180 and a lamp pair placed over the top corners. The MGMT lamps are the guide's own "activity LED and link LED"; BITS lamp roles (Activity left, Link right) are Table 17's

scale.note: drawing - the guide front view (g009860) rendered at 600 dpi measures 2895 x 275 px, aspect 10.53 against the true 482.3/43.7 = 11.04, so the figure is stretched ~4.6% vertically and is SCHEMATIC. All positions below are fractions off it anchored per axis: x at 6.003 px/mm to the 482.3 mm width, y at 6.293 px/mm to the 43.7 mm height. Feature sizes come from the standards registry, never from this drawing. The rear (g009862) is the same art family and was measured the same way

ssd-labels.note: photo - the photographed faceplate labels the 4th and 5th lamps SSD0 then SSD1 left to right; the guide art swaps them. Photo carried

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 4 SFP pairs (port-4/port-5 to port-10/port-11). 4 of these were drawn with the upper cage turned before the std cage art moved its lip to the bottom of the opening; turning them keeps the lips in the middle band where they were drawn and seats every optic bail-outward.

vents.note: drawing - the hex vent fields are drawn as three simplified decor rects using the shared vent pattern; the real punching follows irregular staggered outlines around every feature (including sparse transition runs between the port groups) that are not reproduced hole-for-hole. The small 3-hole columns between the RJ45 jacks are likewise simplified away
